title: Evidence
text: I’ll use the portal to return to Melromarc Castle, set Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs in the incubator… and register their monster crests.
“Kou’s egg too…”

So, after finishing Kou’s registration, I’ll take a look at Sakura-chan’s egg. …Hmm. Sakura-chan is Filolial-sama, who was closest to my Father. After all, he had originally entrusted her with guarding him. I have a vivid memory of how close she was to my Father.

I, Motoyasu, know this. My Father had become a bit reserved because everyone had been helping him level up. If Sakura-chan were here to grow alongside him and protect him, he might be able to let his guard down a little more.

Yeah. Even though she’ll fall a little behind Yuki-chan and the others, let’s keep Sakura-chan around without contracting her as Father’s personal Filolial-sama. It’s a bit of a hassle, but it might be good for Father to grow alongside Sakura-chan. So, let’s have Father register Sakura-chan.
“‘Boo-boo!’”

Hm? I turned around at the sound of some unpleasant squealing, and a pig was pointing at me, squealing as it approached. That completely ruined the happy mood I was in just a moment ago. Stay away, you filthy creature.

As I thought that and looked around, I noticed the sun was already setting quite low. It seems it’s about time I found a place to stay and get some rest. Completely ignoring the pigs, I stashed the egg away and headed for the inn where I’d stayed on the first day.
Later, as I was waiting at my usual nighttime tavern, the Crimson Swine showed up, so after nodding along half-heartedly, I hurled some insults at him.
“Oink! Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!”
That oinking is so noisy. Should I just wipe him out right here and now?

I do think that, but I can easily imagine that if I were to eliminate the Crimson Swine here, it would lead to a future I know nothing about. He’s a piece of Trash, after all. I can guarantee he’ll mock me to my Father—who’s searching for the Crimson Swine after he went missing—calling me a foolish hero who let his comrades escape.

If I’m not careful, he might even make up a story about where I took his daughter and pin a false charge on me. I’ll stick to what my Father said last time. I’ll make a special exception and hold back from taking out the Crimson Swine right now.
“Oink, oink!”
“You’re being persistent. No matter how long you keep squealing, I won’t be fooled by you. You thieving pig!”

“Know this: the only reason you’re still alive is because of my Father’s mercy!” Oink, oink—squealing in response to my insults and seething with rage, Crimson Swine fled the scene. He’s heading straight for Itsuki, I suppose.

Seriously… isn’t there some way to eliminate the Crimson Swine without interfering with the future? It’s frustrating, isn’t it? According to my Father, the Crimson Swine is a tough one to get rid of. If we can avoid war, it might be possible to eliminate him. That’s around the time the Crimson Swine got heavily involved in the commotion, wasn’t it? After that, according to my Father, he curried favor with Ren and Itsuki, and then joined forces with Smoked Meat and the remnants of the Three Heroes Church to launch a revolutionary movement.

So that means… it was after the battle against the Pope. The immediate challenge is how to gain Ren and Itsuki’s trust. Even now, when I think back on the aftermath of that battle, it brings back bitter memories. I charged in thinking I could defeat the Spirit Tortoise, only to let those pigs escape and end up chasing after them for ages.

Chasing after pigs who can’t think of anything but themselves is a waste of time. My spirit was worn down, and… I was encouraged by Filo-tan. After that, I felt a sense of happiness… I awakened to true love.

In that sense, the Crimson Swine was extremely helpful, so let’s execute him painlessly as an act of mercy. We must figure out a way to eliminate the Crimson Swine early on and find a stable foundation free of problems. To put my knowledge of the future to good use… and to put my Father’s words into practice, I must learn the things I was previously unaware of.

If we enter the next loop, what I need to do is find out where my Father, Ren, and Itsuki are within the first few days after I’m summoned. It seems the companions we were introduced to were tasked with subtly keeping my Father and the other heroes at a distance—even going so far as to frame him with false accusations—to prevent them from getting along. During the first loop after the cycle restarted, every attempt I made to get close to my Father was thwarted, but when I acted cool and kept my distance, he simply followed along without incident.

As for the inn, it seems they went ahead and prepared a room for us to stay in on their own. It’s true that they’re interfering to prevent the heroes from coordinating with each other. Father’s specialty is doing things that annoy his opponents—that’s his way of winning a fight. To secure a future where the heroes get along, I’ll be gathering information this time around.

Of course, I have no intention of wasting this loop. After all, I haven’t given up on my dream of finding Filo-tan and becoming her master. There are plenty of ways to make money without making a big move. Well, putting that into action will have to wait a little longer.

Fortunately, since I’d purchased the Filolial-sama eggs from that monster merchant Motoyasu, I can generally tell who’s going to hatch just by the smell and texture. Well, even though the species were different, there weren’t any of Kuu’s eggs during the last loop, so I suppose it depends on the season.

In that case, I’ll just have to visit frequently and keep looking for eggs from Filolial-sama I haven’t encountered before. After all, there weren’t any of Kuro-chan’s eggs during the last loop either, so timing really is crucial.
“Well then… I suppose I’ll get some sleep.”
Back at the inn, I went to bed hugging Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs.

The next morning. As expected, since I’d berated the Crimson Swine, I didn’t get a summons. So, I headed to the castle earlier than I did the time before last. As I approached the castle, the soldiers greeted me with anxious expressions.
“What brings you here so early in the morning?”
“Am I not allowed to come to the castle just for the sake of it?”
“We’re a bit swamped right now, so please come back after the sun has fully risen.”
Just then, Ren and the others arrived in a carriage from behind, looking rather displeased.
“Oh? Isn’t that Motoyasu? Were you summoned too?”
“…Yes, I was.”

It’s better to go along with Ren’s conversation here so I can get in without resorting to force. When I looked at the soldier blocking the path, he turned pale upon realizing he couldn’t possibly ignore me and let Ren into the castle.
“What’s the matter?”
“…Please. Go ahead, Sword Hero.”
“What about Motoyasu? He was summoned just like me, wasn’t he?”
“That’s right, isn’t it? Are you not going to let me in?”
The soldiers are exchanging confused glances. With that kind of attitude, Ren’s going to get suspicious, you know?
“What’s going on? Or is there some reason you’re only calling me and not Motoyasu?”
“No… I understand. Please come this way, Spear Hero.”
“Then I’ll be on my way.”
This is a win. If I time my arrival to coincide with Ren and the others, I won’t have to force my way in.
“Motoyasu, where are your companions?”
“They’re sleeping at the inn. They were sleeping so soundly that I didn’t want to wake them, so I came alone.”
“I see…”
“Where was Ren staying?”
“Me? I was resting in the village two stops past the castle town when I got summoned.”
“I see… Which village, exactly?”
I picture the map of Melromarc in my mind. “Two stops past the castle town” narrows it down quite a bit. Within that range, there are only two or three villages I could reach in a single day.
“That would be—”

It seems Ren had been heading southeast from the castle town. Come to think of it… I just remembered how we discussed things back in the first world to avoid overlapping hunting grounds. I see—I’d better keep that in mind.

Well, since Itsuki has been taken over by the Crimson Swine, it looks like I’ll have to wait a little longer to get any information out of him. As I made my way through the castle and entered the Throne Room, the Crimson Swine, Itsuki, and Trash were waiting there.
“Calling me out this early the very next morning after telling me to set out on my journey… What’s with this sudden summons?”

As soon as they realized I was standing next to Ren, Trash and Itsuki looked distinctly displeased. However, it seemed they prioritized explaining the situation. The Crimson Swine, oozing filth from its eyes and grunting, was speaking to Ren.

This… I’m starting to remember now. If I recall correctly, in the first world, I was standing right where Itsuki is now. Just as I was about to be raped by my Father, the Crimson Swine came running to the inn where I was staying and clung to me, squealing.

After that, the Crimson Swine suggested we report it to the castle, so we went there, where Trash put on a serious act, taking the situation very seriously, and called for Itsuki and Ren. Then the Crimson Swine started wailing things like, “I was almost raped by the Shield Hero. I was so scared…” and “Please, save me from that rapist!” and so on. Her acting was so convincing that both Ren and Itsuki were convinced I was unforgivable.
The Crimson Swine is getting uncomfortably close to Ren, oozing filth while grunting and making a racket. Then the Crimson Swine points at me and squeals.
“Motoyasu, is it true that you called this child a pig?”
“A pig is a pig. Slandering others and covering up misdeeds—if that isn’t a pig, then what is?”
“Covering up misdeeds?”
“Oink, oink.”

When Ren furrowed his brow, the Crimson Swine stepped between me and Ren and tried to shove me aside. But maybe it doesn’t understand how strong I am—it didn’t budge an inch. Hey, you’re supposed to speak human language properly.
You’re probably just spouting some lie anyway. My ears are about to rot from listening to this. I casually keep standing next to Ren. Itsuki has been glaring at me the whole time.
“Is there something you want to say?”
“I’ve been thinking about this since yesterday—what’s with calling a woman a pig?! She’s a human being, you know.”
“Hahaha, you must be joking.”
“What’s so funny?!”
As always, Itsuki’s such a clown. Wearing stolen chainmail and acting all righteous—that’s beyond ridiculous.
“If you really think that, you’d better find out where that chainmail was sold.”
